questionText: We have 2 rectangular sheets of paper, M and N, of dimensions 6 cm x 1 cm each. Sheet M is rolled to form an open cylinder by bringing the short edges of the sheet together. Sheet N is cut into equal square patches and assembled to form the largest possible closed cube. Assuming the ends of the cylinder are closed, the ratio of the volume of the cylinder to that of the cube is ___________
explanation:
1. Volume of the Cylinder (Sheet M):
Sheet M has dimensions $6\text{ cm} \times 1\text{ cm}$.
Rolling it by bringing short edges ($1\text{ cm}$) together gives:
- Height of cylinder, $h = 1\text{ cm}$
- Circumference of circular base, $2\pi r = 6\text{ cm} \implies r = \frac{3}{\pi}\text{ cm}$

Volume of cylinder, $V_{\text{cylinder}} = \pi r^2 h = \pi \times \left(\frac{3}{\pi}\right)^2 \times 1 = \frac{9}{\pi}\text{ cm}^3$.

2. Volume of the Cube (Sheet N):
Sheet N has dimensions $6\text{ cm} \times 1\text{ cm}$.
To make a closed cube, we need $6$ identical square faces.
Cutting Sheet N into $6$ equal $1\text{ cm} \times 1\text{ cm}$ square patches forms a cube with side $a = 1\text{ cm}$.

Volume of cube, $V_{\text{cube}} = a^3 = 1^3 = 1\text{ cm}^3$.

3. Ratio of Volumes:
$\text{Ratio} = \frac{V_{\text{cylinder}}}{V_{\text{cube}}} = \frac{9/\pi}{1} = \frac{9}{\pi}$.

Hence, the correct option is C.
